title: Environment
summary: Pollution is the addition of any substance to the environment in excess of what is normally present, making it impure (from Latin 'polluere', to contaminate). Substances that cause pollution are pollutants: a constituent in the wrong amount, at the wrong place or at the wrong time, e.g. dust, dirt, garbage, chemicals and industrial waste. Pollution is classed as air, water, soil and noise pollution.

Plants give out oxygen by day and use carbon dioxide, balancing the air. Sources: combustion (household fuel, coal in power stations, vehicle exhaust, crackers, factory smoke), industry, agriculture (spraying pesticides and insecticides), solvents and spray paints; natural sources are volcanoes, forest fires and wind-blown dust. Effects: eye infections, respiratory allergies, bronchitis and asthma, skin allergies; plants get less sunlight, their leaf pores are blocked and food production falls; poor visibility and smog cause accidents; rise in temperature and destruction of vegetation (e.g. the Gulf War oil fires).

Control: smokeless chulha with a tall chimney, biogas, solar cooker, chimney filters in factories, factories far from residential areas, devices on vehicles, unleaded petrol and CNG, do not burn garbage (use sanitary landfill), pucca roads, plant and care for trees, grow crops all year so soil is not exposed to erosion.

Safe water has no taste, smell, colour, dirt or germs. Sources of pollution: domestic wastes (washing clothes, bathing animals, washing after defecation, garbage thrown in water), industrial wastes (toxic), agricultural wastes (fertiliser and pesticide run-off), and oil spills. Effects: cholera, typhoid, diarrhoea, dysentery and hepatitis from drinking; skin diseases from bathing; fish and water plants die for lack of oxygen. Control: no untreated sewage or industrial waste in water sources; use latrines; keep latrines, soakage pits, dumping grounds and landfills away from water; no bathing or washing clothes near water sources (harvest rain water for this); no garbage in rivers and seas; a concrete parapet and pucca floor around wells and ponds; store water in clean covered containers and use a long-handled ladle.

Soil pollution is a change in the physical, chemical and biological nature of soil harmful to living beings. Causes: industrial chemicals and metals, excess insecticides, pesticides and fertilisers, rotting garbage that breeds insects and germs, open defecation and urination, spitting. Walking barefoot on such soil lets germs and worms enter the body. Control: proper disposal of garbage in covered bins; dumping pits outside the city covered with soil; sanitary landfills; composting garden waste into manure; incineration (latest technology, expensive but sterile, reduces garbage to ash); burning refuse is banned in metros because of smoke; sanitary latrines, limited use of pesticides and fertilisers and use of Eco-mark (environment-friendly) products.

Any unpleasant sound is noise. Sources: automobiles, trains and aircraft; loudspeakers, radio and TV at full volume; industries and machines. Effects: disturbance, nervous strain, headache, mental disturbance and stress, loss of hearing and deafness (factory workers, pilots, drivers). Control: radio and TV at low volume, avoid loudspeakers, talk in low tones, horns only when necessary, silencers in vehicles, factories and airports away from residential areas.

(i) False. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – CNG is a cleaner fuel and reduces pollution.

or: What are four possible reasons for increase in polluted air in our cities?
Increase in vehicles and their exhaust; smoke from factories and power stations; burning of garbage and household fuel; bursting of crackers; construction dust and cutting of trees.

vsa: Give any four suggestions for safe garbage disposal in your area.
Collect garbage in a covered bin; dump in covered pits outside the city; use sanitary landfills; compost garden waste; incinerate in a furnace; never burn it in the open or throw it into water.

How do oil spills in water bodies affect plant and animal life?
Oil spreads over a large area of the sea and cuts off oxygen, so water plants and animals such as fish die for lack of oxygen and the plant and animal life is badly affected.
Write two measures to control soil pollution.
Proper disposal of garbage in covered bins and landfills; use of sanitary latrines; limited use of pesticides and fertilisers; use of Eco-mark products (any two).
Define pollution and pollutant.

Pollution is the addition of any substance to the environment in excess of what is normally present, making it impure. The substances that cause it, such as dust, garbage, chemicals and industrial waste, are pollutants.
sa: Identify any six reasons for the increase in noise pollution in the world.

Increase in the number of vehicles and their horns; trains and aircraft; loudspeakers at festivals, weddings and political events; radio, TV and music systems played loud; growth of industries and machines; construction work and generators; crowded cities and growing population; factories and airports built near residential areas.

or: Suggest any six ways air can be prevented from getting polluted.

Use smokeless chulha or biogas or solar cooker; chimney filters in factories; factories far from residential areas; fit vehicles with devices and use CNG or unleaded petrol; do not burn garbage; make roads pucca; plant and care for trees; grow crops all year to prevent soil erosion.

sa: Make the villagers aware of the ill effects of air pollution on health. Suggest four ways to control it.

Air pollution causes eye infections, allergies, bronchitis and asthma, and makes breathing difficult; smoke from chullahs affects the eyes and lungs. Control: use a smokeless chulha with a chimney or biogas, use a solar cooker, do not burn garbage and crop residue, plant trees, keep vehicles in good condition.

or: Make your friends aware of the ill effects of water pollution on health. Suggest four ways to control it.

Polluted water causes cholera, typhoid, diarrhoea, dysentery and hepatitis, and skin diseases and allergies. Control: do not let untreated sewage or factory waste into water; use latrines and keep them away from water sources; do not wash clothes or bathe animals in the source; keep water in clean covered containers and use a long-handled ladle.

sa: Briefly describe any three methods of garbage disposal.

Landfill: low-lying land outside the city is used and garbage is dumped daily and covered. Composting: garden garbage is put in a pit and covered with ash and leaves; the lower layers turn into manure. Incineration: garbage is burnt in a furnace; it is sterile and safe and leaves a small heap of ash but is expensive. (Burning in the open causes smoke and is banned in metros.)
la: Describe the sources, effects and any three ways of controlling air pollution.

Sources: combustion of fuel, vehicle exhaust, factory smoke, crackers, pesticide spray, solvents, and natural sources like forest fires and volcanoes. Effects: eye infections, bronchitis, asthma and allergies, poor visibility and smog, less food production in plants, rise in temperature. Control: smokeless chulha or biogas; chimney filters and factories away from houses; CNG and unleaded petrol; planting trees.
Explain how soil gets polluted and suggest five ways to control soil pollution.

Soil is polluted by industrial chemicals and metals, excess pesticides and fertilisers, rotting garbage, and open defecation, urination and spitting, which spread germs and worms; walking barefoot lets them enter the body. Control: (1) dispose of garbage in covered bins and pits; (2) use landfills; (3) compost garden waste; (4) use sanitary latrines; (5) use fewer pesticides and fertilisers; (6) buy Eco-mark products.
